Topic at a glance
Constitutional Foundations of Administrative Law — Articles 14, 19, 21, 32, 226, 300 and 311 is a registered theme in Administrative Law. Constitutional Foundations of Administrative Law — Articles 14, 19, 21, 32, 226, 300 and 311 is governed by constitutional judicial review, administrative law principles, delegated legislation and Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. identify the source of power, statutory duty, decision-maker, affected right, alternative remedy and standard of review applicable to the administrative action.

Provenance, purpose and doctrinal foundation
The topic exists to organise a legally enforceable rule, doctrine or professional procedure. Read the statutory text, constitutional setting, institutional purpose and binding authorities together. The correct analysis begins with the legal question and avoids replacing the governing enactment with a generic textbook summary.

Textual anatomy and operative test
1. Identify the governing enactment, section, article, rule, doctrine or professional standard named by the topic.
2. Deconstruct definitions, conditions precedent, exceptions, provisos, explanations, jurisdictional limits and remedies.
3. Distinguish the topic from its nearest neighbour: Doctrine of Separation of Powers & Rule of Law (Dicey’s formulation); Principles of Natural Justice — Audi Alteram Partem (Right to fair hearing); Principles of Natural Justice — Nemo Judex In Causa Sua (Rule against Bias: Pecuniary, Personal, Subject-Matter).
4. Apply the rule to the record and state which fact satisfies or fails each ingredient.

Courtroom and evidentiary roadmap
Competent forum: the statutory authority or tribunal, High Court under Article 226, Supreme Court under Article 32 or 136 where the constitutional threshold is met, and the competent appellate or review forum. the public authority must act within jurisdiction, follow fair procedure and give a rational, non-arbitrary decision; the challenger must plead the review ground and material facts. Where electronic records are relied upon, apply BSA 2023 s. 63 and the applicable burden provisions without treating electronic admissibility as proof of the ultimate fact. Identify limitation, notice, maintainability, alternative remedy and the exact relief sought.

learningObjectives: Map the principal constitutional controls on administrative action.
Explain how Articles 14, 19 and 21 constrain public power in different doctrinal settings.
Distinguish the remedial roles of Articles 32 and 226.
Analyse property and service protections under Articles 300A and 311 without collapsing them into general judicial review.
enhancement.definition: The constitutional foundations of Indian administrative law are the constitutional limits, remedies and structural guarantees that govern public power, including equality and non-arbitrariness under Article 14, protected freedoms under Article 19, life and personal liberty under Article 21, writ jurisdiction under Articles 32 and 226, the constitutional protection of property under Article 300A, and service safeguards under Article 311.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Administrative action must conform to constitutional supremacy and the governing statutory framework. The intensity and doctrinal route of review depend on the right engaged, the nature of the power, the forum and the statutory context; no single Article supplies a universal formula for every administrative dispute.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India — Articles 14, 19, 21, 32, 226, 300A and 311; the specific statute or rules governing the administrative power.
essentialIngredients: Identify the public power and legal source.
Identify the constitutional right, structural limitation or service/property protection engaged.
Apply the appropriate Article-specific test rather than a generic fairness formula.
Identify the correct writ/forum and maintainability route.
Separate constitutional review from ordinary merits appeal and from statutory service/property remedies.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Article 14 supplies a general constitutional prohibition against arbitrary state action and supports structured equality review. Articles 19 and 21 impose additional substantive and procedural constraints when their fields are engaged. Article 32 is a constitutional remedy for enforcement of fundamental rights, whereas Article 226 confers broader High Court writ jurisdiction for fundamental rights and other legal purposes, subject to its discretionary character. Article 300A protects property through the requirement of authority of law. Article 311 supplies specific safeguards to persons holding civil posts under the Union or a State, subject to its text and recognised exceptions. These provisions operate together but are not interchangeable.
examples: A licensing decision may engage Article 14 even when no Article 19 freedom is directly established on the facts.
A restriction on a protected freedom must be analysed under the constitutional provision governing that freedom, not merely labelled arbitrary.
A property deprivation must be traced to authority of law under Article 300A; the Article does not simply reproduce Article 21.
A disciplinary action against a protected civil servant must be tested against Article 311 and the applicable service law, not only against a generic natural-justice claim.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the administrative act; map the affected constitutional provision; apply its specific test; check the statutory route and alternative remedy; choose Article 32 or 226 only where jurisdiction and maintainability permit; formulate relief proportionate to the constitutional defect.
keyTakeaways: Article 14 is a central control on arbitrary administrative action.
Articles 19 and 21 operate through their own constitutional fields and tests.
Article 32 and Article 226 are distinct remedies with different jurisdictional scopes.
Article 300A is the constitutional property guarantee and requires authority of law for deprivation.
Article 311 provides specific service safeguards and must be read with the applicable service framework.
